source_name: Tracxn — Slovenia fintech company/deal database
why_relevant: Deal-aggregator listing ~136 Slovenian fintech entities with funding status; fastest way to enumerate candidate vendors/competitors and their URLs for downstream monitoring. Directory, not evidence.

source_name: Monri Payments newsroom (CEE PSP, Paypers interview channel)
why_relevant: Regional (Croatia/Adriatic) PSP whose executives publish CEE trend commentary via The Paypers and republish it; a competitor-side window on how Adriatic payment vendors position across Slovenia and Croatia.

source_name: Split Tech City — Adriatic tech/fintech ecosystem coverage
why_relevant: Local Adriatic tech-community publisher producing fintech landscape pieces in English; pointer to smaller regional vendors and events not covered by international trade press.

source_name: Banka Slovenije Fintech Innovation Hub (English pages)
why_relevant: Central bank's English-language fintech hub pages surface which market entrants and solution types are engaging the regulator — an early, non-press signal of vendors preparing to sell into Slovenian banks. Included here because the English pages are what international trade press cites.

source_name: NLB Developer Portal (Odprte storitve NLB) – PSD2 API gallery
why_relevant: NLB's own TPP-facing portal; API specs, sandbox, terms and gateway hostnames expose the underlying API-management/open-banking platform and NextGenPSD2 implementation flavour of Slovenia's largest bank. Changes to spec versions are dated evidence of in-flight integration work.

source_name: Bankart API Developer Portal (openbanking.bankart.si) – multi-bank PSD2 hub
why_relevant: Single hub hosting PSD2 sandboxes/production APIs for many Slovenian banks. Its existence itself is vendor evidence: Bankart is the shared processing/open-banking platform provider. Per-bank sub-portals enumerate which banks outsource open banking to Bankart vs. run their own — a near-complete map of the SI open-banking vendor landscape.

source_name: Addiko Bank Slovenija Open API developer portal
why_relevant: Addiko runs its own (group-level) open-banking stack rather than the Bankart hub — the portal's branding, URL scheme and API-gateway fingerprints indicate the vendor/platform used across the Addiko group.

source_name: Intesa Sanpaolo Open Banking group portal – Slovenian ASPSP (Intesa Sanpaolo Bank Slovenija) API docs
why_relevant: Shows Intesa's Slovenian subsidiary served from the Italian group open-banking platform — group-centralised vendor decisions, and the doc set names the NextGenPSD2 profile and certificate/test flow.

source_name: OTP banka d.d. (Slovenija) PSD2 / TPP pages
why_relevant: Bank-side PSD2 landing page that points onward to the actual technical portal (Bankart tenant) — a pointer-plus-direct source revealing which processor OTP SI uses post-merger with SKB/Nova KBM, and when it switches.

source_name: Sparkasse Slovenija – Odprto bančništvo / API PSD2
why_relevant: Slovenian-language PSD2 page that explicitly routes TPPs to openbanking.bankart.si/sparkasse — dated, documentary proof of the outsourced open-banking vendor.

source_name: Gorenjska banka – Odprto bančništvo PSD2
why_relevant: Points to the bank's Bankart tenant (openbanking.bankart.si/gbkr) and states the eIDAS/Berlin Group profile; useful for tracking whether AIK-group ownership shifts the technical stack.

source_name: Delavska hranilnica PSD2 API product pages on Bankart hub (SRC PSD2 API Collection)
why_relevant: Strongest single weak-signal example found: the API product description names the 'SRC PSD2 API Collection' — i.e. the Slovenian integrator SRC d.o.o. as the implementation vendor behind a bank's PSD2 interface. Exactly the kind of vendor exposure that never appears in press releases.

source_name: UniCredit group developer portal (developer.unicredit.eu) – Slovenia ASPSP entry
why_relevant: UniCredit Banka Slovenija is served by the group PSD2 platform; portal newsroom/FAQ carry dated release notes and country-specific exemption/technical notices for SI.

source_name: Open Banking Tracker – Slovenia country page
why_relevant: Aggregator listing SI ASPSPs with their developer portals — fastest way to enumerate every Slovenian bank API portal and spot new/changed ones; third-party curation so treat as lead list, not truth.

source_name: Google Play listing – NLB mKlik (package id ba.asseco.android.ae.nlbbl)
why_relevant: Textbook indirect vendor signal: the Android package identifier itself contains 'asseco', exposing Asseco as the mobile-banking platform vendor for an NLB-group bank. Package ids, developer account names and 'What's new' notes are dated, un-suppressible vendor evidence across all SI banking apps.

source_name: Bankart careers page and individual job ads (zaposlitev)
why_relevant: Bankart is the shared SI card/payment processor; its job ads for 'razvojni inženir analitik', POS business analysts and Linux system engineers name technologies, product lines (ATM, POS, wallets, SEPA SCT/SDD, instant) and hint at in-flight modernisation projects months before announcements.

source_name: Optius.com – company job-ad pages (e.g. NLB d.d.)
why_relevant: Slovenian job board with per-company landing pages; bank IT ads there name platforms, languages and integration stacks. Company pages make it easy to track a single bank's hiring wave (a proxy for programme start dates).

source_name: MojeDelo.com – Slovenian job board (IT / banking ads)
why_relevant: The largest SI commercial job portal; bank and integrator IT ads are the primary place a named core-banking, card-management or payment-hub platform is disclosed. Referenced repeatedly as a main portal alongside Optius.

source_name: ZRSZ / ESS – Zavod RS za zaposlovanje official vacancy search
why_relevant: State employment service vacancy register — employers must publish many vacancies here, so it is the least suppressible, most complete national job-ad corpus, including bank IT roles that never reach commercial boards.

source_name: Careerjet.si – aggregated bank job ads (SI)
why_relevant: Aggregator that pulls ads from many SI boards and company sites into one queryable stream, including per-company views (e.g. NLB) — efficient sweep layer that surfaces ads on boards not otherwise monitored.

source_name: Zaposlitev.info – SI job board (banking/payments roles)
why_relevant: Carries bank payment-domain roles (e.g. a 'samostojni sodelavec za razvoj poslovanja na področju plačilnega prometa' ad) whose text describes payment product roadmaps and systems in use.

source_name: Borza dela (borzadela.si) – employer-scoped vacancy search
why_relevant: Secondary SI board with employer-name URL patterns; useful redundancy for capturing bank IT ads that appear briefly and are then removed.

source_name: LinkedIn company pages of SI banks/processors (e.g. Bankart d.o.o.)
why_relevant: Employee skill/title profiles and job posts expose named platforms (core banking, card management, API gateway) and, in aggregate, headcount shifts around implementation programmes — often earlier and more specifically than any public announcement.

source_name: Bankart Flik product & support pages (Flik Pay / Flik POS)
why_relevant: Flik is the national instant-payment scheme operated by Bankart; product, support and terms pages plus the participating-bank lists reveal which banks are live on which Bankart services and when they join — de-facto deployment evidence.

source_name: Slo-Tech forum – IT/banking threads (app releases, salaries, stack chatter)
why_relevant: Slovenian technical community where bank app rewrites, outages and employer stacks are dissected by practitioners, sometimes insiders; low individual reliability but very high early-signal value and useful for naming vendors/platforms to then verify.

source_name: Vsezamojdan.si – consumer tech coverage of SI bank app releases
why_relevant: Consistently reports SI bank app updates in detail (login flow changes, push-authentication replacing SMS OTP, NLB Pay feature drops) — effectively a dated, indexed narration of release notes, which is easier to monitor than store listings.

source_name: NLB Group press-release archive as corroboration layer for digital-channel releases
why_relevant: Not a weak signal itself, but the dating anchor: comparing the press-release date of a digital-channel launch (e.g. the unified NLB Klik) with earlier job ads and app-store version history quantifies how many months ahead the indirect signals fire.
